question: When is an exception plan prepared?
options: When requested by the board after an exception
At the start of every management stage
Only after the project has closed
Whenever a team member asks, without examining the forecast
explanation: It is not an automatic plan for each stage.

question: Where is the decision to authorize the next stage made?
options: Directing a project
Controlling a stage
Managing product delivery
Managing a stage boundary
explanation: Managing a stage boundary supplies information; the board directs.

question: Who prepares the next stage plan?
options: Project manager
Team manager
Project board
Project executive
explanation: Stage boundary work prepares the next stage for authorization.

question: Who authorizes the next stage?
options: Project board
Project manager
Team manager
Project executive
explanation: The board makes the go or stop decision.

question: Which report compares the completed beta with its approved plan?
options: End stage report
Checkpoint report
Highlight report
Exception report
explanation: The report records performance and lessons.

question: Why should the business case be reviewed at the boundary?
options: To check whether the project remains justified
Use the next stage plan in place of the revised business case
Prepare an exception plan for every normal stage boundary
Use an exception report as the authorized replacement plan
explanation: Updated costs and benefits inform further investment.

question: Which plan shows the current forecast of the complete project?
options: Project plan
Stage plan
Team plan
Exception plan

question: The board asks for a replacement plan after an exception. What is prepared?
options: Exception plan for the board to consider
Use the next stage plan in place of the revised business case
Prepare an exception plan for every normal stage boundary
Use an exception report as the authorized replacement plan
explanation: An exception plan can replace the affected plan after approval.

question: What distinguishes an exception report from an exception plan?
options: The report escalates a forecast breach; the plan sets out replacement work
Checkpoint report
Highlight report
Exception report

question: What evidence does Maya provide at the stage boundary?
options: User test outcomes and acceptance information
Use the next stage plan in place of the revised business case
Prepare an exception plan for every normal stage boundary
Use an exception report as the authorized replacement plan
explanation: User feedback informs the next decision.

question: What justifies asking the board to authorize another stage?
options: Updated stage assessment, next stage plan and business case
Project plan
Quality register
Daily log
explanation: The board needs evidence of viability and a realistic plan.

question: When is a stage plan developed in detail?
options: Before that stage, usually at the preceding boundary
At the start of every management stage
Only after the project has closed
Whenever a team member asks, without examining the forecast
explanation: Near term planning is more reliable.

question: What is a useful result of lessons learned in the preceding stage?
options: Better estimates and controls for the next stage
Treat the updated project plan as authorization of the next stage
Ask the team manager to approve a replacement stage plan
Omit the end stage report when the stage is within tolerance
explanation: Lessons inform the next stage plan.

question: Beta results cast doubt on expected benefits. What should the project manager do?
options: Update the business case and present the assessment to the board
Use the next stage plan in place of the revised business case
Prepare an exception plan for every normal stage boundary
Use an exception report as the authorized replacement plan
explanation: The board decides whether to continue investing.
